sources.entry: TinyFeed - Generate a static HTML page from a collection of feeds with a simple CLI. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: tinyfeed is a CLI tool that turns a list of RSS, Atom, or JSON feed URLs into a single static HTML page.
summary.what_it_does: The tool takes a list of feed URLs and generates one HTML page aggregating their entries. It requires no database and no config file, only the CLI and HTML templates. The README says it can be scheduled with crond, systemd, or openrc to regenerate the page. It supports RSS, Atom, and JSON feeds through the gofeed library. Output can be customized with external stylesheets and templates. The page uses a dark or light theme based on system preference, and a daemon mode can regenerate the output periodically.
use_cases: aggregate RSS feeds into one webpage
generate a static news page from blogs
view multiple Atom or JSON feeds in one place
schedule periodic feed digests with cron or systemd
notable: Static HTML output with no database or config file
Supports RSS, Atom and JSON feeds
Built-in daemon mode for periodic regeneration
Light and dark theme following system preference
caveats: Installation, usage, and customization details are only in an external documentation website, not in the README
Live demo and screenshot content is referenced but not reproduced in the README
